### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, touching **4** documentable anchor(s).

**2** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/data-modeling/validation.mdx`  _(via SeedLoaderService (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/protocol/objectql/state-machine.mdx`  _(via SeedLoaderService (symbol, a top-level class))_

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-1.mdx`  _(via SeedLoaderService (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `organization_id (literal, 34 pages)`
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **11** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a2a3777bf53855f2e9ca43f1bcfa2623c561a224` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `06c9e0e7292422b8e8e2566f3f1979a09096f6fd` — the merge of head `7cfdef026d6fc58a21231195e34d7457b6d39445` into base `a2a3777bf53855f2e9ca43f1bcfa2623c561a224`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 06c9e0e7292422b8e8e2566f3f1979a09096f6fd && git checkout 06c9e0e7292422b8e8e2566f3f1979a09096f6fd
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin a2a3777bf53855f2e9ca43f1bcfa2623c561a224 7cfdef026d6fc58a21231195e34d7457b6d39445 && git checkout -B drift-repro a2a3777bf53855f2e9ca43f1bcfa2623c561a224 && git merge --no-ff 7cfdef026d6fc58a21231195e34d7457b6d39445

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a2a3777bf53855f2e9ca43f1bcfa2623c561a224
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs a2a3777bf53855f2e9ca43f1bcfa2623c561a224` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `7cfdef026d6fc58a21231195e34d7457b6d39445`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/metadata-protocol/src/seed-loader.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/seed-loader-null-organization-holder.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/seed-loader-null-organization-holder-real-driver.integration.test.ts, scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json + packages/spec/src/data/seed-loader.zod.ts (`ReferenceResolutionErrorSchema`, the result's `errors` array), packages/spec/src/data/data-engine.zod.ts (`EngineQueryOptions`), packages/objectql/src/engine.ts (`toDriverOptions`: `hasTenant` needs `execCtx.tenantId`), packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin.ts (`isSystem` bypass in the middleware and `getReadFilter`) and tenant-layer.ts (the Layer 0 wall), packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver.ts (`whereNull`, `applyTenantScope` unscoped without `tenantId`), packages/runtime/src/app-plugin.ts (the `seed-replayer` closure), packages/cloud-connection/src/marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts (`runInlineSeed`, the walled install door, the healer, `buildSeedReplayer`), packages/plugins/organizations/src/organizations-plugin.ts (the replay's error count and samples), packages/runtime/src/domains/packages.ts and packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts (unscoped callers), packages/runtime/src/seed-replay-per-organization-identity.integration.test.ts (the sibling real-driver pin), scripts/check-engine-double-contract.mjs, scripts/check-driver-memory-census.mjs, scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs, scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs, scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs, docs/adr/0131-total-organization-ownership-no-null-organization-id.md (D9, D10 fate 4, D12), docs/adr/0087 (the `no-migration-prescription` category). The `.changeset/24301-seed-null-organization-holder-refused.md` prose face is judged under ②.

Inputs read: card #24301's body and all four comments (triage 6249042739, claim 6251425947, dispatch 6251443381, `os-dev-report` 6252574758, the last read as claims only), parent #24282, decision #24352 and its ruling comment 6251599171, epic #15194's body; PR #24372's body and file list; the net diff `git diff a2a3777bf53855f2e9ca43f1bcfa2623c561a224 pr/24372` (5 files, +673/−2; merge base = the PR's recorded base); the check-runs on the head. Nothing built, run or re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

**The accept-set change, named.** On an organization-scoped load (`config.organizationId` set) in `upsert` or `ignore` mode, not a dry run, a seed record whose natural key no row of that organization holds but a row with `organization_id` NULL does hold is now REFUSED: `errored++`, one `ReferenceResolutionError` pushed to `errors` and `allErrors`, `success: false`, one `logger.error` line per dataset. Before, `loadExistingRecords` read `where: { organization_id: ORG }` only, the NULL holder was invisible, `decideWriteAction` answered `insert`, and a twin carrying the organization landed with 0 errors (the premise still holds on `origin/main`, seed-loader.ts line 3138). Right, and it is exactly the card's Done when.

- **Which rows, which modes.** `unownedHolders` is created only inside the pre-load branch, `if (config.organizationId && mode !== 'update') unownedHolders = new Map()` (seed-loader.ts ~1013), so only scoped `upsert`/`ignore` make the NULL read. `decideWriteAction` refuses only when `!existing && (mode === 'upsert' || mode === 'ignore')` and the key is in the map. `update` never inserts: an unmatched key is `skip` as before, no NULL read is made (pinned: "update mode writes no new row"). `insert`/`replace` never pre-load and never consult the map, so a scoped `insert` over a NULL-held key still inserts, as it inserts over any held key: that is the mode's own semantics, outside the card's Done when, and the PR says so in its Acceptance notes. Right. A dry run makes no pre-load and therefore does not predict the refusal; not in the Done when, noted for the seat.
- **Never adopted, never returned as the organization's own.** The NULL read adds a key to `unownedHolders` only when `!map.has(key)`, and never to the returned map, so `existingRecords` (the one source for `update`/`skip` and for `insertedRecords`/`noteLanded`) never carries an unowned row. A refused record `continue`s before the early-signal `decideWriteAction` call (~1745), the batched decision (~1814) and the self-referencing `writeRecord` call, so neither write path, the reference map (`insertedRecords`) nor the seed-settlement report (`recordOrganizationReplay(ctx, organizationId, result.results)` in app-plugin.ts, fed by `noteLanded`) ever sees it. `engine.update` is never called on the holder (unit pin). The rechecks in `writeBatchPartial` (~1132) and `writeOne` (~1176) call `loadExistingRecords(objectName, externalId, config.organizationId)` with no map, so they read `organization_id = ORG` only (unit pins: one NULL read per load, the retry's recheck `where` is `{ organization_id: ORG }`, no insert payload carries a held key). Passing the map there would have returned the unowned row as a committed outcome and put its id in the reference map: adoption by another door. Keeping them scoped is right. The organization's own row wins when both hold a key (unit pin). The refused rows' deferred references are reported as dropped by pass 2 because the reference DB probe is itself organization-scoped (`where.organization_id = organizationId`, ~2131), so no link is ever pointed at an unowned row (real-driver pin, the cascade). Right.
- **Other organizations stay invisible; the read is bounded by predicate, not by key.** The scoped read is `organization_id = ORG` and the NULL read is `organization_id IS NULL` (sql-driver.ts compiles a null comparand through `whereNull`, lines ~16634 and ~17064, the same Knex path on SQLite, Postgres and MySQL); a row stamped with another organization matches neither, and `if (record?.organization_id != null) continue` is a second guard against a driver that treated `{ k: null }` as no predicate. Real-driver pin: OTHER_ORG's row holding the key stays untouched and this organization gets its own row. Cost: ONE extra `engine.find` per dataset (per object, not per row), full rows, no `fields`, no `limit`: it is not bounded to the keys the load needs. On a 17.x database where every row is NULL it reads the whole table once per dataset. That is the same unbounded shape as the existing pre-load (which reads every row of the organization, full columns, to compare no-op replays), so it doubles a known cost rather than adding a new class of it. Acceptable; noted.
- **The elevated context.** The NULL read carries `context: { isSystem: true }` and no `tenantId`, like every other read in this file (the pre-load, `isRowIdHeld`, `resolveSoleOrganizationId`, the reference probes). In `ObjectQL.toDriverOptions` `hasTenant` requires `execCtx.tenantId !== undefined`, so no `tenantId` reaches the driver and `applyTenantScope` leaves the read unscoped by its own contract; the security plugin's middleware returns `next()` on `isSystem` and `getReadFilter` answers `undefined`, so the Layer 0 wall is not AND-composed. It is therefore a genuine cross-tenant system read, bounded only by the IS NULL predicate: by construction it can see every unowned row of the object and nothing stamped. What reaches a caller: only the holder's `id` (`extractId(unowned)`), in the message of the refusal. The full unowned row stays in the map and is never returned, matched, written or re-pointed. The row belongs to no tenant and the remedy (find and attribute it) needs its id. Right.
- **Unscoped load and a fully stamped database.** With no `config.organizationId` the map is never created, the pre-load keeps its unscoped read (no `where`) and still matches the NULL row, so the single-posture boot keeps adopting by match as before, 0 inserts on a seeded database (unit pin "an unscoped load reads no NULL holders"; real-driver pin "an unscoped (single-posture) load keeps its behaviour", 2 inserts for the two unheld keys only). A fully stamped database loads with 0 inserts and 0 errors (real-driver pin). Both as the Done when requires. Right.
- **Every scoped caller.** The production `seed-replayer` (app-plugin.ts ~1840: `defaultMode: 'upsert', multiPass: true, organizationId`, returning `errors: result.errors`) is pinned through the real closure a walled `AppPlugin` boot registers (real-driver test, `tenancy: { posture: 'isolated' }`); its consumer, organizations-plugin.ts ~423-432, logs `errors.length` and samples `errors.slice(0, 5)`, so the refusal reaches the operator's log with its message. The walled install (marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts ~3258-3273: `runInlineSeed(ctx, datasets, organizationId)` under `organizationWallActive`, logging `errors=N` and carrying `errorSample`), the reseed endpoint and the marketplace's own replayer (`buildSeedReplayer`, returning `errorList`) all build the identical request `{ defaultMode: 'upsert', multiPass: true, organizationId }`; the real-driver test pins that request shape directly, not by executing `runInlineSeed` (it lives in `packages/cloud-connection`, outside the claim's surface). The loader reads nothing but the request, so the pin reaches those callers; a drift in `runInlineSeed`'s own config would not be caught by it, which is the one soft spot and is acceptable at this surface. The rehydrate-time healer (~879, `runInlineSeed(ctx, datasets)`), the package apply (`packages.ts` ~2724), the publish-time load (`protocol.ts` ~25580) and the inline boot seed and hot reload (app-plugin.ts ~1938, ~2316) pass no `organizationId` and are unchanged. `standalone-stack.ts` constructs no `SeedLoaderService` and names no organization; there is no scoped caller there.
- **The error shape.** `ReferenceResolutionErrorSchema` describes "an actionable error for a failed reference resolution", and this refusal is not one. But the result schema has `errors: z.array(ReferenceResolutionErrorSchema)` and no other per-row shape, and the loader already carries three non-reference failures in it: the `(expression)` error, every engine write failure (`buildWriteError`, "the same ReferenceResolutionError shape a failed write has always"), and the ADR-0131 D9 unowned-row refusal (`field: 'organization_id'`, `targetObject: 'sys_organization'`, `targetField: 'id'`, `attemptedValue: null`). The shape is de facto the seed result's one per-row error carrier; the schema prose predates and already misdescribes those. The new entry is at least as honest: `targetField` really is the externalId field used for matching, `attemptedValue` really is the key value that failed to resolve to a row this organization owns, and the message names the object, record, key, holder id, the NULL ownership and the remedy. The structural tell (`field === 'organization_id'` and `targetObject === sourceObject`) tells it apart from the D9 refusal (`targetObject` is `sys_organization`), and both pins read it that way. Every reader (the replayer consumers, `runInlineSeed`) reads `errors.length`, `message` and samples; none branches on a kind. A discriminator would be a `packages/spec` change with no consumer. Reuse is right; the dev's open question resolves to its option A.
- **Territory and decision #24352.** #15194's declared territory (stage 9: plugin-sharing, the cli ceremony inventory/apply, `standalone-stack-seeder-declaration-copy.test.ts`, `security-catalog.ts`; C8: engine.ts tenant derivation, `platform-object-tenancy.ts`, `tenant-layer.ts`, `sql-driver.ts` `applyTenantScope`, driver-turso, the chokepoint gate, the named NULL readers) contains no path of this diff. The new `organization_id IS NULL` read is a NULL reading of a kind, not one C8 names; after NOT NULL it returns nothing and is harmless, and `check-tenant-chokepoint.mjs` does not census it. Decision #24352 ruled C: an unattributable NULL row blocks certification and the ceremony never guesses an owner (D10 fate 4). The loader refuses, never adopts, and names the ceremony (`os migrate organization-ownership`, then `--apply`) as the remedy: consistent with C and with D10. Once 8c-0 lands, a database that keeps such rows is not served at all; this refusal is then the second guard for NULL rows of any other origin, which is the card's stated purpose. No contradiction.

### ② Semver level

The changeset bumps `'@objectstack/metadata-protocol': minor` with a `fix(metadata-protocol)!:` title, the line `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, a `**BREAKING** (a seed load writes fewer rows), shipped as minor under the launch-window convention` banner, FROM/TO/Unchanged paragraphs and the one-line remedy. That is the level the repo's own rule prescribes: `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` reads a declared `narrowing` as BREAKING that ships `minor` during the launch window, and the three #24210 narrowing changesets on `main` use the identical spelling. The ADR-0087 disposition is `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` with its why: nothing an author writes and no stored shape is added, removed, renamed or converted; the change is which rows a load writes, the NULL rows' attribution is the ceremony's, and the result keeps its shape. The FROM/TO lines describe behaviour (inserted vs refused), not a key rewrite, and the remedy names the operator ceremony, not `objectstack migrate meta`, so the body carries no prescription the detector refuses; the "Check Changeset" job on this head (pr-automation.yml, `check-adr-0087-registration.mjs --base MERGE_BASE`) passed. The PR body carries `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` followed by a parenthetical reason, the same line as the claim; `readClause2Line` reads the value and the arm and tolerates trailing prose, and the dispatch-gates lint passed. The bump is on the one package whose source changed; the runtime test file publishes nothing. Level and declarations are right.

### ③ Boundary flags

1. **Real-driver pin in `packages/runtime/src`, outside the claim's file list.** Justified: `@objectstack/objectql` depends on `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, so the loader's package cannot reach a real engine and driver without a cycle, and the sibling pin `seed-replay-per-organization-identity.integration.test.ts` already lives there for the same reason. A test file only; no runtime source, no `seed-replayer`, no `@objectstack/verify` touched. Accepted. The seat should amend the claim's File surface to name the file (the dev's own recommendation on its fourth open question).
2. **`scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json`, 3 rows.** The gate's ledger is regenerated with `--write` and never hand-edited; the new fake declares `delete`, `findOne` and `update` through `assertEngineDeleteDispatch`, `assertEngineUpdateDispatch` and `assertEngineFindOnePredicate` from `@objectstack/metadata-core`, which is what the rows pin; the "Lint & Repo Gates" family (lint.yml runs `pnpm check:engine-double-contract`) passed on the head. Accepted.
3. **Postgres measured once, not pinned.** The permanent pin is SQLite only; the "Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)" job skipped by path filter. The code path is the evidence: a null comparand compiles through the same Knex `whereNull` on every SQL dialect, and the loader's `!= null` filter holds whatever a driver answers. The dev's "4 passed on PG 16" is a claim and is treated as one. Accepted.
4. **Memory driver dropped from the pin for `check:driver-memory-census`.** The gate requires every `@objectstack/driver-memory` declaration to be ledgered; dropping the arm is the right disposal. The unit fake reads `{ f: null }` as IS NULL and throws on any `$` operator, so the `$or` shape the PR rejected would have failed it; the memory driver's own NULL semantics stay unpinned, and the loader does not depend on them. Accepted.
5. **The shared checkout detached and re-attached.** A process deviation from the worktree rule; the report says no edit was made in it and the diff shows none. For the seat's record; no effect on the head.
6. **Five pushes, no REST writes beyond PR + report.** Within the dispatch.
7. **Open questions.** (a) Error shape: option A, reuse, judged honest above; no `domain:spec` declaration owed. (b) Rechecks: option A, scoped only, judged right above; B would adopt. (c) Modes: option A; `update` makes no twin, `insert`/`replace` are the mode's semantics; the card asked for the twin. (d) Pin placement: option A, with the claim's File surface to be amended by the seat.
8. **Noted, not blocking.** The NULL read is per dataset, full rows, unbounded by key (same shape as the existing pre-load). A dry run does not predict the refusal. Logged once per dataset while every refusal is counted and reported, matching the D9 refusal's convention.

**Check-runs on the head, as read.** 39 check-runs: at the last read 30 `success`, 6 `skipped` (Build Docs, Temporal Conformance live PG + MySQL, Dogfood Regression Gate shards, Dogfood Verify CLI, Console Pin Gate, Packed-tarball smoke; all path-filtered), 3 `in_progress` (Test Core 2/6, 3/6, 4/6; shards 1/6, 5/6 and 6/6 had completed `success` between the first and second read). Green at the read: TypeScript Type Check, Lint & Repo Gates, Build Core, every Lint and Type Check family, Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Check PR Size, the three claim/branch guards. The landing still requires every check green; the three shards are the gate's to finish, not this record's to presume.
